title: Toy Story 2
tagline: Snatched by a collector. Fed by the gang.
about: Woody is stolen by a toy collector and the gang sets out to rescue him.
cue: Serve the cheese puffs when Al takes Woody home to his apartment.

    StartersAl's cheese puffsBaked choux puffs with cheddar and gruyère, light and crispHow to make it125ml water50g butter75g plain flour2 eggs50g vintage cheddar40g gruyèreBoil the water with the butter, beat in the flour and cook a minute.Cool, beat in the eggs, then the grated vintage cheddar and gruyère.Pipe small rounds and bake at 200°C until puffed.Woody's Roundup smoky cowboy beansBacon beans for Woody's Finest Hour.How to make itAs written, serves 4Beans slow-cooked with smoky bacon, onion, molasses, mustard and tomato until thick and sticky, served in tin mugs with cheesy cornbread crumbs.Fry 200g diced bacon until crisp, add 1 diced onion and cook 5 minutes.Stir in 2 x 400g tins drained cannellini beans, 400g tinned tomatoes, 2 tbsp molasses, 1 tbsp Dijon mustard, 1 tsp smoked paprika and 250ml water.Cover and bake at 160°C for 90 minutes, stirring once.Crumble 2 cornbread muffins with 40g cheddar and toast under the grill to scatter on top.MainsProspector's chilliSlow braised beef chuck chilli with chipotle and kidney beans, sour cream, cornbreadHow to make it1.2kg beef chuck1 brown onion3 garlic cloves2 chipotles in adobo2 tsp ground cumin2 tins of crushed tomatoes2 tins of kidney beans200g sour cream1 packet cornbread mixDice the beef, onion and garlic.Brown the beef in batches.Add the onion, garlic, chipotles and cumin, then the tomatoes and drained beans. Braise until tender.Bake the cornbread as the packet says.Serve with sour cream and squares of cornbread.Al's Toy Barn honey butter fried chickenBuck-buck-buck! And that's cheap-cheap-cheap!How to make itAs written, serves 4Buttermilk-brined drumsticks double-dredged and fried crunchy, drizzled with honey butter, with creamy coleslaw and pickles on the side.Soak 12 drumsticks overnight in 500ml buttermilk with 1 tsp salt.Mix 250g plain flour with 2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder and salt.Dredge, dip back in buttermilk and dredge again.Fry at 165°C for 12 to 14 minutes until 75°C inside.Melt 50g butter with 3 tbsp honey and drizzle over.Toss half a shredded cabbage and 1 carrot with 120g mayonnaise and vinegar.SweetsJessie's yodelling cookiesCutout sugar cookies shaped like hats and boots, iced in cowgirl coloursHow to make it125g butter100g caster sugar1 egg250g plain flour300g icing sugar1 egg whitered food colouring, a few dropsBeat the butter and sugar with the egg, then mix in the flour.Chill the dough.Roll and cut into cowboy hats and boots.Bake at 180°C.Mix the icing sugar with the egg white, tint some red and ice the cooled cookies in cowgirl colours.Bullseye's caramel apple wedgesApple wedges dipped in caramel and rolled in crushed roasted peanutsHow to make it200g caramels2 tbsp thickened cream3 apples60g roasted peanutsMelt the caramels with the cream until smooth.Cut the apples into wedges and pat dry. Crush the peanuts.Dip the wedges halfway and roll in peanuts, then set on baking paper in the fridge.DrinksJessie's yee-haw sarsaparilla floatSarsaparilla over vanilla ice cream and caramel, served with long spoonsHow to make it4 tbsp caramel sauce8 scoops of vanilla ice cream1.3 L sarsaparilla4 hat-shaped biscuitsChill four tall glasses.Drizzle caramel sauce down the inside of each glass and add ice cream.Pour sarsaparilla slowly down the side, letting the foam settle before topping up.Perch a biscuit on each rim and serve with long spoons and straws.
